pairs.why: Both trains have similar soft key-light form turns and glossy black boilers with no meaningful lighting difference from the reals.
Both docks are lit alike, with sunny flat water and similar post shading and cast shadows, so nothing on lighting separates them.
B has smoother soles and a softer, deeper form shadow under the straps like the real flip-flops, while A's dense dot texture breaks up the form turn.
A has the real cards' deeper core shadows, a warm glow behind the subject and crisp rim and sheen on the leather, while B is pale and flatly lit.
A has a broader soft cast shadow and more rounded, saturated form shading on the glass and liquid, while B reads as a photoreal glass with fussy speculars.
A has the soft broad sheen and gentle shadow depth of the real player, while B has sharper hot spots, a glossier plastic look and heavier orange bounce.
A has the real fins' glossy yellow sheen, a deep core shadow and a warm rim, while B is matte and flat-lit with a slightly textured surface.
A has a bit more form-shadow depth and rim glow on the target and bear, while B is flatter, though the two are close.
